asset.name: Solana

score_rationales.institutional: Solana has achieved meaningful institutional depth: spot ETFs from Fidelity, BlackRock, VanEck, and others crossed $1.45B in cumulative inflows since October 2025 launch, Goldman Sachs disclosed $108M in SOL holdings, Visa and BlackRock BUIDL are active on-chain, and ~17.9M SOL sits in publicly-traded corporate treasuries — but overall ETF AUM and corporate treasury breadth remain well below Bitcoin's tier, keeping the score in the high-70s range.
score_rationales.regulatory: SOL's regulatory trajectory has materially improved in 2025 — the SEC dropped enforcement actions that had named SOL as a security (Coinbase, Kraken cases), and multiple spot SOL ETF applications (VanEck, 21Shares, Canary Capital) are in active review under a pro-crypto SEC chair, signaling institutional legitimacy; however, no formal legal-status ruling has been issued, ETF approval remains pending, and EU/UK frameworks have not explicitly cleared SOL, leaving meaningful jurisdictional ambiguity that caps the score.
score_rationales.supply: SOL has no supply cap and carries ~4.68% annual inflation (SIMD-228 failed in March 2025, preserving the fixed dilution schedule), which creates ongoing structural sell pressure; however, 92.3% of total supply is already circulating, meaning VC/team overhang is minimal. A strong offset comes from 68% of supply being staked (~393M SOL), materially compressing the tradeable float and keeping APY incentives intact at ~5.86%. The exchange-reserve picture is the primary drag: Glassnode data shows net-positive exchange inflows on every session in April 2026, signalling distribution rather than accumulation, though the concurrent $202M outflow capitulation signal introduces a contrarian element that moderates the bearish read.

score_rationales.adoption_activity: Solana shows elite network adoption in May 2026: ~3.9M daily active addresses (dominant across L1s), $8B+ DeFi TVL, $3.8B+ daily DEX volume (#1 cross-chain), 3,000–5,000 real TPS with sub-$0.001 fees, and 17,700+ active developers — the largest cohort across blockchains; only slight discount from 100 reflects TVL pullback from its $12.2B ATH.
